title: Pointwise left Kan extensions have the mapping-space universal property
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent diagrams, transformations, functor categories, mapping spaces, and colimiting cocones as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in fixed sufficiently large universes. Let $C,D$ be quasicategories, $K$ a small simplicial set, $\delta:K\to C$ and $F_0:K\to D$ diagrams, $F:C\to D$ a functor, and $\beta:F_0\to F\delta$ a coherent transformation. For $c\in C$, let $C_{/c}$ be the simplicial set whose $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to C$ taking the last vertex to $c$, with projection to $C$ by the first face; the join concatenates the vertices of its two factors in that order. Put $K_{/c}=K\times_C C_{/c}$. Suppose that for every $c$ the coherent cocone on $K_{/c}$ induced by $\beta$ and the universal arrows $\delta k\to c$, whose legs are
$$F_0(k)\xrightarrow{\beta_k}F(\delta k)\xrightarrow{F(u)}F(c),\qquad u:\delta k\to c,$$
is colimiting. Then for every functor $G:C\to D$, restriction followed by composition with $\beta$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,D)}(F,G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(F_0,G\delta),\qquad \alpha\longmapsto(\alpha\delta)\beta.$$
This concerns the full coherent transformation spaces and is natural in $G$. No other colimits in $D$ are assumed to exist.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.3.6.1 (0309), with pointwise left Kan extensions defined in Variant 7.3.1.5 (02YC). The comma indexing simplicial set and its cocone are written out here rather than left as a notion defined only by tag. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags; read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-inner-horn-completion] to the given small simplicial set $K$. It supplies a small quasicategory $\widehat K$ and $i:K\hookrightarrow\widehat K$ for which restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(\widehat K,X)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)$ lifts every monomorphism for every quasicategory $X$ in the containing universe. Lift the vertex $\delta$ for $X=C$, obtaining $\widehat\delta$, and lift $F_0$ for $X=D$, obtaining $\widehat F_0$. For $X=D$, apply the same lifting property to $\partial\Delta^1\subseteq\Delta^1$, with endpoints $\widehat F_0,F\widehat\delta$ upstairs and the edge $\beta$ downstairs. This gives an edge $\widehat\beta$ with these exact endpoints and restriction $\beta$. By [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pointwise-lan-invariance], the assumed pointwise colimit property on $K$ implies the same property for $(\widehat\delta,\widehat F_0,F,\widehat\beta)$ on $\widehat K$. In particular the replacement preserves the specified unit, not just the objects of the diagrams.

source.place: Opening reduction to a quasicategory index; Change of Diagram, Proposition 7.3.1.14.

proof.text: For any fixed $G$, write $M_X(a,b)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(X,D)}(a,b)$ and $U_X(a,b)=U_{\operatorname{Fun}(X,D)}(a,b)$. The restriction $U_{\widehat K}(\widehat F_0,G\widehat\delta)\to U_K(F_0,G\delta)$ lifts every monomorphism $A\subseteq B$: a proposed lift is precisely a lifting problem for the functor-category restriction in Step 1 on $(A\times\Delta^1)\cup(B\times\partial\Delta^1)\subseteq B\times\Delta^1$, with the two endpoint diagrams prescribed. It is a homotopy equivalence: lifting $\varnothing\subseteq U_K$ gives a section, and lifting $U_{\widehat K}\times\partial\Delta^1\subseteq U_{\widehat K}\times\Delta^1$ over the constant image gives a homotopy between its composite with restriction and the identity. The natural pinch equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] therefore make $M_{\widehat K}\to M_K$ a homotopy equivalence as well. Restriction of triangles and pinch maps commutes, so the composition characterization of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] gives $[\theta_K]=[i^*][\theta_{\widehat K}]$, since $\widehat\beta|_K=\beta$. It suffices to prove the conclusion with $K$ a quasicategory; rename the extended data $K,\delta,F_0,\beta$.

source.place: Opening reduction: equivalence on the entire target transformation space, not only on vertices.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-join-left-kan-reduction]. Set $E=K\star_C C$, with its two full inclusions $j_0:K\to E$, $j_1:C\to E$, structure map $r:E\to C$, and $h:\Delta^1\times K\to E$. Choose the supplied realization $\bar F$ restricting exactly to $F_0,F$. Its edge $\bar\beta=\bar Fh$ has the same fixed-endpoint homotopy class as $\beta$, and its canonical cocones make $\bar F$ left Kan extended from $j_0K$. For each $G$ put $\bar G=Gr$; the same lemma gives the local limit cones making $\bar G$ right Kan extended from $j_1C$. It also gives $\bar Gh$ identically constant at $G\delta$. The left and right properties concern the specific local cocones and cones, so no existence of arbitrary colimits or limits in $D$ has been introduced. The composition rule of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] allows $\beta$ to be replaced by $\bar\beta$ in computing the homotopy class of $\theta$.

source.place: Relative-join reduction, Proposition 7.3.2.11, and recognition of G-bar as right Kan extended.

proof.text:
Put $Z=U_E(\bar F,\bar G)$. Apply [lem-coef-full-subcategory-kan-trivial-restriction] first to the full inclusion $j_0K\subseteq E$, using the local colimit condition on $\bar F$, and then to $j_1C\subseteq E$, using the local limit condition on $\bar G$. It gives actual restriction maps
$$a:Z\longrightarrow U_C(F,G),\qquad b:Z\longrightarrow U_K(F_0,G\delta)$$
that are trivial Kan fibrations and homotopy equivalences. Let $q:U_C(F,G)\to U_K(F\delta,G\delta)$ be restriction along $\delta$. Thus $qa$ is literally restriction to $j_1\delta$. Both applications have full inclusions and quasicategory targets by Step 3; the lemma requires the Kan property of the indicated source or target functor only, not that every diagram on the subcategory admit an extension.

source.place: The two trivial-fibration restriction maps phi-plus and phi-minus.

proof.text:
For an $n$-simplex $z$ of $Z$, write its arrow family as $	au_z:\Delta^n	imes\Delta^1	imes E	o D$, whose time endpoints are $ ar F, ar G$. Define the square family
$$W_z(s,t,v,k)=	au_z(s,t,h(v,k)).$$
Its four sides, with the entire $\Delta^n$ parameter retained, are: $t=0$ is the constant family $ ar eta$; $v=1$ is $(qa)(z)$; $v=0$ is $b(z)$; and $t=1$ is the degenerate identity of $G\delta$, because $ ar Gh$ is constant. Restrict this square to the two monotone triangles with vertices $((0,0),(0,1),(1,1))$ and $((0,0),(1,0),(1,1))$ in the $(t,v)$ coordinates. source.place: The final homotopy-commutative triangle, expanded in the fixed-endpoint arrow model by the two triangles of the naturality square.

proof.text: Use the characterization of composition by the short-edge map $\vartheta:V\to U\times U$ and long-edge map $\ell$ in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. For $\rho_L$, it gives $[d]=[\text{compose with }\bar\beta][qa]$. For $\rho_R$, it gives $[d]=[\text{compose with identity}][b]=[b]$ by the unit law. Hence the entire maps satisfy $[b]=[\theta_U][a]$ in the homotopy category of Kan complexes, where $\theta_U$ is the comparison in the arrow model. Since $a,b$ are homotopy equivalences, $[\theta_U]=[b][a]^{-1}$ is invertible. The natural pinch equivalences in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] and the composition formula identify this with the stated comparison on right-pinched mapping spaces. Restore the original index by Step 2. This proves the asserted equivalence of spaces without constructing an inverse componentwise or identifying pointwise equalities with equality of transformations.

source.place: Homotopy commutativity and the two restriction equivalences imply that theta is an equivalence.

proof.text: Finally retain $G$ as a variable. The operation $G\mapsto Gr$ is precomposition by the fixed simplicial map $r$, and both $a,b$ are the restrictions themselves. Their coherent naturality is included in [lem-coef-full-subcategory-kan-trivial-restriction], applied to this family; it applies to all $Gr$ because Step 3 proves its right Kan condition for every $G$. The square in Step 5 is precomposition by the fixed map $(t,v,k)\mapsto(t,h(v,k))$, and its two triangle inclusions do not involve $G$. In any additional simplex parameter $\Delta^p$, all three operations keep that factor by its identity map; restriction along $\mu:[q]\to[p]$ gives equal composites because $(\mu\times1)(1\times T)=(1\times T)(\mu\times1)$ for each fixed square or triangle map $T$. Thus the comparison of the natural restriction span with composition by $\bar\beta$ retains the higher parameter data. Pinch maps are natural under simplicial functors by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], and composition is the triangle-space operation of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. The resulting equivalence is therefore natural in $G$. The preliminary index restriction is fixed independently of $G$, so the same naturality holds for the original $K$.

source.place: Naturality in G via the restriction span, the parameter-preserving square, and natural pinch maps.

Kerodon is not archived locally, so I read these tags online: 0309 (the statement and the whole proof route), 030M, 02YZ and 02YL. The item statement matches Kerodon Prop 7.3.6.1: K is an arbitrary simplicial set, beta is specific, the pointwise condition is on K/c, and no extra colimits are assumed. The steps follow Kerodon's proof. Step 1 replaces K by an inner-horn completion: the lifting property of lem-coef-small-inner-horn-completion lifts delta, F0 and beta with fixed endpoints, and the inner-anodyne invariance node (Kerodon 02YL(2)) keeps the colimit hypothesis. Step 2 shows restriction on transformation spaces is a trivial fibration via the monomorphism (A x Delta1) u (B x dDelta1) in B x Delta1. Steps 3-4 use the relative-join node (Kerodon 02YZ plus 024J/02FK, including the exact identity that Gr composed with h is constant) and then the full-subcategory theorem twice (Kerodon 030M, either/or hypothesis). In Step 5 I recomputed all four sides of the square, its vertices and both triangles: the edge pairs are (qa, beta-bar) and (id, b), with the same diagonal d. Step 6 gives [b] = [theta_U][a] through the composition formula and its unit law; Step 7 gives naturality in G. The new nodes are statement-only, self-contained and searched, with correct blueprint fields. I tested them on edge cases: A=C, A empty, K empty, delta = identity, and the horn inside Delta2. The cycle check (BFS) is clean, all citations stay in the item's unit, and no SGA source is used. lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction is a weaker near-duplicate of the new full-subcategory node, but its dependencies reach this item, so it cannot be cited here and the new node is justified. I suggest the maintainer later re-derive that node from the new one. No fixes.
